prompt: What does a log-based counter metric record each minute?

choices.text: How many entries matched its filter
choices.why: Right. Nothing else about the entry is kept, except extracted labels.

choices.text: The text of every entry that matched
choices.why: The entries stay in the log bucket; the metric keeps a number.

choices.text: The total since the metric was created, growing for ever
choices.why: It is DELTA, a count per interval, never cumulative.

choices.text: The severity of the worst entry
choices.why: Severity can be filtered on; it is not what is counted.

prompt: In checkout.log, 14:01 has no matching line. What does the counter record for that minute?

choices.text: A point of zero
choices.why: No entry, no point: absence is not zero.

choices.text: The previous minute's value, repeated
choices.why: Nothing is carried forward.

choices.text: No point at all
choices.why: Right. Lesson 14 shows why that matters to an alert.

choices.text: An error, because the metric found nothing
choices.why: Finding nothing is normal and silent.

prompt: A team adds the order id as a label on the retry counter. What happens?
hint: Every distinct value is its own series.

choices.text: Nothing changes: labels are free
choices.why: Each series is billed and queried on its own.

choices.text: One series per order: costly and slow
choices.why: Right. Unbounded label values are the commonest mistake.

choices.text: The metric refuses labels with more than ten values
choices.why: There is no such small limit; that is why it gets expensive.

choices.text: Retries become easier to alert on
choices.why: An alert wants the total, which is now scattered over thousands of series.

prompt: Add the counter's points from 14:12 to 14:17 inclusive (12, 15, 18, 13, 16, 11). How many retries happened in the bad patch?
Why look at the values in the log before declaring a distribution's buckets?

choices.text: Cloud Monitoring needs exactly one bucket per value
choices.why: Any bounds are accepted; good ones keep the data's shape.

choices.text: Buckets are fixed when the metric is created
choices.why: Right. Changing them means a new metric.

choices.text: Values outside the buckets are deleted from the log
choices.why: The log is untouched; outliers land in the overflow bucket.

choices.text: The bucket bounds decide which entries match
choices.why: The filter decides matching; buckets only histogram the value.

prompt: What makes `shop/order_value_cents` a distribution rather than a counter?
hint: It reads a number out of each entry.

choices.text: Its filter on "order placed"
choices.why: A counter could use the same filter.

choices.text: Its name ending in _cents
choices.why: A name decides nothing.

choices.text: value_extractor with DISTRIBUTION and buckets
choices.why: Right. The extracted number is what is histogrammed.

choices.text: metric_kind = "DELTA"
choices.why: The retry counter is DELTA too.

prompt: Lesson 9 excludes successful `/healthz` entries. A counter of healthz requests is then created in the same project. What does it count?
hint: Does an excluded entry reach the metric?

choices.text: Every health check, since metrics read before exclusions
choices.why: The lesson says the opposite: excluded entries are never counted.

choices.text: Only the failed ones; the excluded ones never reach it
choices.why: Right. A contradiction no plan catches.

choices.text: Nothing: the plan refuses to create it
choices.why: The plan sees no conflict; both are valid alone.

choices.text: Every check, twice
choices.why: Nothing doubles; the exclusion removes them.

prompt: What opens an incident in a log-based alert policy?

choices.text: A rate above a threshold for five minutes
choices.why: That is a metric condition, lesson 14.

choices.text: Ten matching entries in an hour
choices.why: Counting is a metric's job.

choices.text: One entry matching the filter
choices.why: Right. One line is enough.

choices.text: A person marking an entry as important
choices.why: Nobody marks entries; the filter decides.

prompt: Why does the break-glass policy carry `notification_rate_limit`?
hint: A log alert fires once per matching entry.

choices.text: To delay the first notification by five minutes
choices.why: The first goes at once; the limit caps the ones after it.

choices.text: So ten retries do not send ten messages
choices.why: Right. And Cloud Monitoring requires it on log alerts.

choices.text: To close the incident after five minutes
choices.why: Closing is auto_close, half an hour here.

choices.text: To keep the policy inside the free tier
choices.why: It is about people, not price.

prompt: The break-glass policy as written in this lesson is applied. A break-glass deployment happens. Who is told?
hint: Read the policy for a channel.

choices.text: The project's owners, by e-mail
choices.why: No channel names them; nothing is sent by default.

choices.text: Whoever made the deployment
choices.why: The policy knows no such person.

choices.text: Nobody: an incident opens, and no channel is named
choices.why: Right. Lesson 14 adds the channels.

choices.text: Google support
choices.why: Your alerts are not sent to Google.

prompt: Match each question to the tool that answers it.

pairs.left: Is this happening more than usual?
pairs.right: a counter and an alert on its rate

prompt: The field of `google_logging_metric` that takes a label's value out of each entry is `label____`.
hint: A plural word, after the underscore.

prompt: Put the path of a "payment retried" line to a point on a chart in order.
hint: The line is written before anything counts it.
items: The API writes the JSON line
The entry is stored in a log bucket
The counter's filter matches it and its label is extracted
The minute's point is written to Cloud Monitoring
trap: Counting before the entry is stored is the slip: an excluded entry is never counted.

prompt: Both payment methods retried in similar numbers during the bad patch. What does that suggest?
hint: What would one provider failing look like?

choices.text: The pix provider failed
choices.why: Card retried just as much.

choices.text: The label extractor is broken
choices.why: Both values came out as expected.

choices.text: A cause upstream of both
choices.why: Right. The checkout's own call, not one provider.

choices.text: Nothing: retries are normal
choices.why: Ten times the background is not normal.
